newsitem.title: UK: West African markets steady to firmer, Med quiet.
newsitem.headline: West African markets steady to firmer, Med quiet.

text.p: Crude oil markets in the Mediterraean were quiet as refiners stayed away from expensive Urals but West African grades were steady to firmer as U.S. and other buying mopped up most of the first decade barrels.
In the Mediterranean, buying interest was stifled as refiners held back from paying the strong numbers asked for Urals by the two traders holding most of the barrels.

Traders said the key to the crudes price was the speed with which Iraqi crude came back on to the market. One trader noted that should the 180 day period for the renewed deal start from June 8 as expected, then the Mediterranean market would "be flooded" with the grade as most U.S. and Eastern buying had already been completed up to the end of July.
On Tuesday, U.N. officials and Western diplomats said it was likely Iraq would pump its $2.14 billion sales quota in a condensed time period driving production volumes higher once sales resumed.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Wednesday that Iraq would resume oil exports as soon as the distribution plan under the oil for food plan with the U.N. was completed.

Syrian state oil company Sytrol was heard to have made its first offer to contract holders on Wednesday. The company was looking to increase the differential for its light grade crude from dated Brent -77 cents in June to dated Brent -55 cents in July. Contract holders were heard well below this level.
